title: Section 24 HMA — Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings

content.overview: Section 24 empowers the court, in any proceeding under the Act, to order the respondent to pay the petitioner maintenance pendente lite and such expenses of the proceeding as appear reasonable if it appears that the petitioner has no independent income sufficient for support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding.
content.study: Either spouse may apply; the focus is relative financial capacity and necessity during the litigation, not final property division. Quantum is discretionary and fact-sensitive. Distinguish from permanent alimony and maintenance under section 25, which usually follows or accompanies a decree under the Act. Pair with sections 9, 13, and 13B as the host proceedings.

learningObjectives: Explain Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 24 and its statutory purpose.
Identify and apply the provision's ingredients to a factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related HMA remedies.
enhancement.definition: Section 24 empowers the court in proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act to order maintenance pendente lite and reasonable litigation expenses where the statutory financial condition is satisfied.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 24 is interim financial relief during matrimonial proceedings. The court considers the applicant's independent income, support needs, litigation expenses and the financial circumstances of both parties.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 24; read with the particular matrimonial proceeding and the court's discretionary assessment.
essentialIngredients: There must be a proceeding under the Act.
The applicant must lack independent income sufficient for support and necessary proceeding expenses.
The court must assess reasonable maintenance and litigation expenses.
The relief is discretionary and fact-sensitive.
Relevant financial disclosure and conduct may affect the determination.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 24 is designed to prevent financial inequality from undermining participation in matrimonial litigation. It is distinct from permanent alimony under Section 25. The Supreme Court's recent Sukhdev Singh decision confirms that Section 24 relief is discretionary and that conduct can be considered while applying the statutory conditions.
examples: A spouse without sufficient independent income applies for interim maintenance during a pending HMA proceeding. The court assesses income, needs, liabilities and litigation expenses before fixing an appropriate amount.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 24 concerns pendente lite maintenance and litigation expenses; Section 25 concerns permanent alimony/maintenance at or after a decree.

caseLaw.name: Sukhdev Singh v. Sukhbir Kaur
caseLaw.citation: Civil Appeal Nos. 2536 and 5726 of 2019; order dated 4 June 2026
caseLaw.holding: Order dated 4 June 2026. The Court recorded the answers of the larger bench dated 12 February 2025, including that even if a court reaches a prima facie conclusion that the marriage is void or voidable, it is not precluded from granting maintenance pendente lite under Section 24 if the conditions in that section are satisfied, and that relief under Section 24 is discretionary and the conduct of the party seeking relief is considered. This order set aside the impugned orders to the extent they dealt with interim alimony under Section 24 and permanent alimony under Section 25, and remitted those questions to the Additional District Judge, Amritsar / Family Court, without interfering with the decree under Section 11.
caseLaw.relevance: Opened order applying Section 24 to proceedings arising from a marriage declared void under Section 11, and remitting the interim-maintenance question.

enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the host HMA proceeding, compare each spouse's income and resources, assess reasonable needs and expenses, and apply the court's discretion under Section 24.
